content: Cracker Barrel operates a chain of 557 establishments, as of 2007, known as Old Country Stores. These locations combine a retail store and a restaurant, and they are spread across 41 states in the United States, with the company headquartered in Tennessee. The Cracker Barrel chain specializes in serving traditional Southern comfort food. Historically, their outlets have been located along interstate highways, although this policy appears to be evolving. Breakfast is available throughout the day, but the breakfast menu is distinct from the lunch and dinner menu. Both menus include a section dedicated to low-carbohydrate options. The exterior porch of a Cracker Barrel store features rows of rocking chairs for guests to relax before or after their meals. Inside the dining area, there is often a fireplace and a checkers set to enhance the rustic, country ambiance. The interior walls of the dining area are adorned with antiques, including photographs, advertisements, and household items. The retail store primarily sells nostalgic merchandise, collectibles, housewares, crafts, toys, classic candies, and items used in preparing Cracker Barrel entrees. In 1991, Cracker Barrel implemented a policy requiring employees to exhibit normal heterosexual values, which the company claimed were foundational to family structures in society. During the 1990s, the company reportedly terminated at least 11 gay employees. Despite protests from gay rights groups, the company initially refused to alter its policy. However, in 2002, after a historic proxy vote by shareholders—led by the New York City Employees Retirement System, a major shareholder—58% voted to rescind the policy. Following this, the board of directors added sexual orientation to the company’s non-discrimination policy. In the early 2000s and again in 2006, Cracker Barrel faced allegations of racial discrimination in its treatment of customers. After these accusations gained national media attention, the company introduced explicit policies to address the concerns. While prominent critics ceased their public criticisms, Cracker Barrel ultimately paid $2 million to settle claims of racial and sexual harassment at three Illinois restaurants. The company now displays signs in its front foyers clarifying its non-discrimination policy, a practice adopted after a similar incident involving Denny’s restaurants. In March 2006, Cracker Barrel agreed to pay $2 million to settle class-action allegations of sexual and racial discrimination brought by the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC v. Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc.). In October 2006, Rose Rock, the mother of comedian Chris Rock, threatened legal action against Cracker Barrel after alleging that she and her daughter were discriminated against at the company’s Murrells Inlet, South Carolina, restaurant. She claimed they were not served for over an hour and that when she inquired about the delay, the manager offered a free meal instead of investigating the issue, which she declined. Cracker Barrel was also one of eight companies accused of making illegal corporate campaign contributions to the Texans for a Republican Majority Political Action Committee (TRMPAC), founded by Representative Tom DeLay. However, less than five months later, all charges against Cracker Barrel were dropped. On February 2, 2005, the District Attorney stated that there was no intent on Cracker Barrel’s part to violate any laws and acknowledged the company’s history of good citizenship and high ethical standards. Cracker Barrel admitted no wrongdoing but agreed to make a $50,000 charitable contribution to support a nonpartisan, balanced, and publicly informative program at the LBJ School of Public Affairs at the University of Texas-Austin. This contribution was intended to reinforce the company’s longstanding commitment to good corporate citizenship and proper participation in the political process. In May 2007, Cracker Barrel temporarily removed hamburgers from its menu at most locations after a customer in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, reportedly found a metal fragment resembling part of a razor blade in her hamburger.
